S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (PDD), or dysthymia, is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a depressed mood lasting at least two years in adults, accompanied by additional depressive features and clinically significant distress or impairment. Compared with major depressive disorder, PDD tends to have a more insidious onset, a longer and more stable course, and symptoms that are less severe but more enduring, often becoming embedded in a person's sense of self. Patients frequently present with long‑standing low mood, low energy, and pessimism that they may describe as their "normal" way of being, leading to underrecognition and delayed treatment. Comorbidity with major depressive episodes (double depression), anxiety disorders, and medical conditions is common, and functional impairment can be substantial despite relatively mild to moderate symptom intensity at any given time.

patient.personality: Emely is a disciplined, quietly competitive farm worker who channels her love of organization and sustainability into meticulous record‑keeping, careful budgeting, and ambitious long‑term plans.
patient.stressor: Just over three years ago, Emely’s marriage ended after a prolonged period of conflict over money, long work hours, and her desire to eventually start her own sustainable produce venture, leading to a divorce that left her living alone and shouldering most financial responsibilities. She threw herself into work on the regional farm, using spreadsheets, safety checks, and crop planning as a way to stay focused, while privately watching peers advance into supervisory roles or build families, which sharpened her sense that she was falling behind. As seasons passed with repeated setbacks—missed promotions, a failed attempt to secure a small loan for her own project, and ongoing tension with her ex‑partner over shared obligations—her belief that her efforts could change her future gradually eroded, and she began to treat her careful plans more as rituals than as realistic pathways. When she realized that even activities she once found grounding, like her personal garden, book club, and desert hikes, now felt like going through the motions, and coworkers commented on how unlike herself she seemed in meetings and safety audits, she finally accepted a referral from a community clinic to see a psychiatrist, fearful that her growing sense of futility was starting to jeopardize both her work and her remaining relationships.
patient.chief_complaint: “I just don’t see any future for myself anymore, no matter how hard I try.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days it feels like there’s a gray film over everything, like I’m just going through my chores on the farm and even when the crops look good or someone cracks a joke, inside I feel flat and heavy, and I sometimes end up crying alone in the truck for no clear reason on my lunch break.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how early I go to bed, I wake up already worn out, and just walking the rows, lifting crates, or even sitting down to update my spreadsheets feels like I’m dragging a body that’s twice as heavy as it should be, so by the time I get home I barely have the strength to heat up something simple and lie on the couch.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: Somewhere along the way I stopped believing that working hard or planning ahead would actually change anything, so now when I look at my budgets or my notes for starting a small produce business, it just feels like I’m pretending, because in my gut I’m sure I’ll never get the promotion, never get the loan, never have a family, and that this is as good as my life is ever going to get.
